svg.text: LEFT WALL · TEAK, A LITTLE MODERN
SEEN FROM THE ROOM · ENTRANCE DOOR D1 ON THE LEFT · STUDY BOOKCASE END ON THE RIGHT · DASHED LINE = PARTITION (APPROX.)
EVERY IDEA CARRIES THE STUDY COUNTER LINE (570–610) AS A REEDED TEAK STRIP · 9 FT CEILING · SIZES ARE ESTIMATES
1 · YOUR IDEA — TEAK TO ONE THIRD
Teak wainscot to 915 (3 ft) with long mouldings and a cap; the counter line runs through it as a reed
Good, but on a 9 ft wall the wood reads low and the plain wall above feels big — as you suspected
2 · TEAK TO THE TOP OF THE DOOR
Wood runs up to the head of D1 — the strongest line on the wall — with long moulded panels; plain band above
Recommended: timeless, lines up with the door and the counter, and the plain band keeps it light
Full-height teak veneer in wide boards with fine V-joints, no mouldings; shadow gaps at floor and ceiling
The most modern — very calm, lets the grain do the work; a lot of wood beside the bookcase
Painted wall, recessed shadow-gap skirting and a single teak reed on the counter line; one large artwork, picture light
Cheapest and quietest — lets the desk, bookcase and right wall carry the room
